note: Day after the draft, preseason Week 3 (no games count yet). Roster is full at 15, no waiver has run, full 100 FAAB. Nothing on the wire is a clear upgrade over the current bench, so no add is recommended today. The one build-relevant idea is a Jonathan Taylor handcuff (I roster JT with zero insurance), held on WATCH until the IND RB2 split breaks. Own-roster watch items: Emeka Egbuka (toe) and Sam LaPorta (hip), both Week-1 uncertain per the news file; Jake Ferguson already covers LaPorta at TE.

targets.why: The Colts have talked openly about managing Jonathan Taylor after his league-high 323 carries, and Giddens is listed RB2 on the first unofficial depth chart, with rookie Seth McGowan generating the camp buzz and leading Sleeper adds. Whoever wins the job is a direct handcuff to a workhorse who would hand his backup a weekly-starter role if he ever missed time. (IND depth chart, Aug 2026)
targets.asset: Contingent RB1 workload if Taylor misses time; otherwise minimal standalone touches behind a workhorse.
targets.my_team_impact: I roster Jonathan Taylor (RB1) with no handcuff, my only real insurance gap. In a 5-bench league his backup is a league-swinger if JT misses time. An add would cost a deep WR dart (Quentin Johnston or Ja'Kobi Lane), neither of whom cracks my starting 10.
targets.worth: FAAB 3-5 ceiling as cheap workhorse insurance, decayed only lightly with a full season ahead.
targets.confidence_why: IND RB2 is an unsettled Giddens-vs-McGowan split; the handcuff is not locked to one player, which caps confidence regardless of the clean insurance logic. Buying the wrong half is dead weight.
targets.competition: Seth McGowan (rookie, leading Sleeper adds and camp buzz); both unrostered in-league. No rival owns Taylor, so nobody is racing me for his handcuff.
targets.bid: 0 now, WATCH. Claim the winner for FAAB 2-3 (routine, uncontested) once the final preseason game clarifies the RB2 job; no bidding pressure since no rival owns Taylor.
targets.drop: Quentin Johnston or Ja'Kobi Lane, my two deepest WR darts; neither cracks the starting 10.

targets.why: Direct handcuff to Josh Jacobs, whose NFL personal-conduct investigation (May 2026 domestic-disturbance call, no charges) is still open with a six-game floor for a first violation and more discipline expected before Week 1. If Jacobs is suspended, Lloyd inherits a bell-cow role in a strong offense. (nfl-events, Aug 19)
targets.asset: Contingent bell-cow RB1 if Jacobs is suspended or hurt; otherwise a stash with no standalone role.
targets.my_team_impact: No synergy with my roster, I do not own Jacobs. Purely speculating on another team's player losing time, and it would cost a bench spot I would rather keep on my own Jeanty/JT contingencies and WR darts.
targets.worth: FAAB 1-2 as a pure lottery ticket for me; near-zero unless I am punting a bench spot.
targets.confidence_why: Binary on a suspension ruling with no timeline, and the payoff accrues to Jacobs' owner (Stipe), not to me.
targets.competition: Stipe owns Jacobs and has no handcuff; if a suspension drops, expect a frenzy bid (60+ floor per the FAAB model's injury-replacement history). Unrostered now.
targets.bid: 0, not my add. Flagging it as the league's next frenzy target the day any Jacobs suspension is announced; I am not the buyer unless I have a bench spot to burn.

targets.why: Rookie running with Miami's first team in a WR room hollowed out by the Tyreek Hill release and the Jaylen Waddle trade to Denver, a genuinely open competition with no established No. 1 (~27k Sleeper adds). (MIA depth chart, Aug 2026)
targets.asset: Speculative WR3/flex if he wins the target lead, but in a low-ceiling Malik Willis offense.
targets.my_team_impact: Roughly lateral to Ja'Kobi Lane on my bench, a deep WR dart with no locked role and a worse quarterback. Does not crack my starting 10 and is not a clear upgrade over what I already hold.
targets.worth: FAAB 1-2, a dart, not an upgrade.
targets.confidence_why: Wide-open room, unproven rookie, Malik Willis at QB, low target certainty in a low-ceiling environment.
targets.competition: Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell (same open room); unrostered in-league.
targets.bid: Pass. My own WR darts (Odunze, Johnston, Lane) are better-situated.

targets.confidence_why: Target share split with Dell and a returning Jaylin Noel behind Collins; role unproven.
targets.competition: Tank Dell, Jaylin Noel (same vacated targets); unrostered in-league.
